android.desc:
Since 2002, Three Rings has made it easy to manage volunteers and rotas at charities around the world. From your desktop, laptop, tablet or smartphone, view and share shifts, volunteer details, news, events, files, and more with others in your charity/non-profit organisation.

Your organisation will need to have a Three Rings account before you can use this app. If they don't already, they can sign up for a free trial at https://www.threerings.org.uk/.

Our volunteer-run team welcomes your feedback: email support@threerings.org.uk to get in touch.

quotes.text:
It's possible, but I think it's more likely that the Google account that has made the Three Rings app (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=uk.org.threerings.pwa) with a listed phone number (+44 7795...) also claimed ownership of the Three Rings website through whatever domain tools Google offers.

In that case, the developer provided Google with a way for Three Rings customers to reach them and they then published that number.

I don't know why the app's developers decided to use their personal phone number for their Google Play business contact information, but that seems like the most reasonable explanation to me.

If the author did not provide that phone number to Google Play, then he will need to also update his information there to get the phone number delisted, or it will be a matter of time before it appears on the Google Search page again.
